clips.start_words: So if you have in your ancestors
clips.caption:
Somewhere in your bloodline, someone got hurt and made a silent vow: never again.

That vow didn't end with them. Trauma your ancestors carried — a woman cheated on, a man betrayed — can sit encoded in your own DNA, running as a program you never agreed to: "I don't trust men," "women always lie," quietly deciding who you let close before you even speak. This isn't a theory. Researchers are now confirming trauma passes down in the DNA itself, generation after generation, until someone finally clears it.

Comment RISE and I'll send you how to start.

#subconscious #epigenetics #awakening #consciousness #ancestraltrauma #kevintrudeau

People write in convinced their partner finally changed.

They didn't. Clear the counter-intention sitting in your own field and the other person doesn't need to do a single thing differently, because it was never really about them. Whatever you were carrying is what had been running the whole dynamic. Fix the broadcast and the relationship you're receiving shifts with it, instantly, without a conversation or an argument.

Comment RISE and I'll send you how this actually works.

#awakening #consciousness #subconscious #manifestation #relationships #kevintrudeau

Somewhere you picked up the idea that there's exactly one right person out there for you.

Run the odds. Out of every person alive, the chance there's only one who could give you a passionate, communicative, secure relationship isn't just unlikely, it's close to impossible. What's actually true is simpler and kinder: there are many people you could build that life with. The pressure of finding "the one" is optional, and it's been working against you.

Comment RISE and I'll send you the rest of this.

#manifestation #relationships #awakening #consciousness #mindset #kevintrudeau

"You complete me" sounds romantic. It's actually a warning sign.

If you need someone else to feel whole, you're not in a relationship, you're in a dependency wearing a relationship's clothes. Two whole people come together and create a third thing, an "us," without either person disappearing into the other. That's why when you catch yourself saying "I love us," you're naming something real: a separate entity the two of you built together, not a hole one person filled in the other.

Comment RISE and I'll send you the rest of this teaching.
